title: Add retention policy config resources/modules for Private deployments
author: Vivek Kulkarni
description: Summary: Adds Terraform resources and a small helper module to configure retention controls for Redwood Private deployments where the control plane supports the retention policy service (policy schema v1.1). This is intended to reduce Security/GRC friction during enterprise onboarding by making retention configuration auditable, repeatable, and exportable. Motivation: Several Private design partners requested “infrastructure as code” for retention defaults and per-tenant overrides to align with internal change control. This PR wires up policy CRUD via the retention policy API and provides safe-by-default validation consistent with the control plane schema (min/max TTLs per tier enforced server-side; Terraform additionally validates basic shape for faster feedback). Scope: - New resource: redwood_retention_policy (create/update/delete + read) - New resource: redwood_retention_policy_attachment (attach policy to tenant/logging config where supported) - New data source: redwood_retention_policy (lookup by name/id) - New module: modules/retention_policy_private (opinionated defaults + examples) - Docs: provider docs + examples for common regulated profiles (short request-log retention + longer audit-log retention) Behavior notes: - Private-only: resources require provider config `deployment_mode = "private"` (or equivalent) and will error clearly in Hosted/Dedicated. - Legal hold is intentionally not modeled as a Terraform switch in v1; holds are handled via break-glass workflow and audited operations (see Security guidance). - Deletions are “policy object deletion” only; actual data purge is handled by server-side TTL enforcement jobs. Terraform deletion will remove the policy reference; it does not guarantee immediate physical deletion of already-stored data. - Update semantics: changes produce a new policy revision server-side (change history kept); Terraform diffs only show the desired current config. Example usage: `resource "redwood_retention_policy" "regulated" { name = "regulated-default" data_class { kind = "audit_logs" ttl_days = 365 } data_class { kind = "request_response_logs" ttl_days = 14 } data_class { kind = "traces" ttl_days = 30 } }` and attachment via `redwood_retention_policy_attachment` (tenant_id + policy_id). Testing: - Unit tests for schema normalization + diff suppression for unordered data_class blocks - Acceptance-style tests gated behind `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT` and `REDWOOD_PRIVATE_TOKEN` (skipped in PR CI, run nightly) - Local verification steps documented in docs. Rollout: No breaking changes to existing provider behavior. Users may optionally adopt the new module; existing logging_config resources remain supported. Follow-ups: - Add import examples for existing policies (tracked separately) - Expand module to cover per-region overrides once control plane enables it for Private (future work).

resource: add retention policy attachment to tenant logging config
docs: add retention policy examples for Private deployments

review_conversation: Benji Okafor: Can we align the Terraform-side validation errors with the control plane messages? In particular the min/max TTL wording and the “unsupported data class” case. Vivek Kulkarni: Updated validators to mirror server enums and to surface `unsupported data class` with the same list of allowed kinds; TTL min/max now points users to server-enforced limits and includes the tier/deployment note. Ethan Park: Attachment resource worries me—are we coupling to logging config internals? We should make it clear this is a best-effort helper and will no-op / error cleanly if the Private control plane doesn’t expose the attachment endpoint. Vivek Kulkarni: Added capability check on provider configure; attachment resource returns a clear diagnostic when `retention_policy_attachment` capability is absent. Also updated docs with the required minimum Private version. Marcus Lin: Please add a note about legal hold not being managed by Terraform and why; we’ve had customers try to encode holds into IaC, which conflicts with approval/audit requirements. Vivek Kulkarni: Added explicit docs section “Legal hold (not supported via Terraform)” and linked to internal workflow. Sean Gallagher: Acceptance tests being skipped is fine, but can we add a nightly job note and a local runbook snippet? Also watch for plans that churn due to ordering of data_class blocks. Vivek Kulkarni: Added diff suppression + stable sort on expand/flatten; docs now include local acceptance instructions and mention nightly. Approvals: Ethan Park approved after capability gating changes. Marcus Lin approved after docs clarification. Benji Okafor approved after validation updates. Sean Gallagher approved after diff suppression + testing notes.
release_notes: Terraform provider: Add `redwood_retention_policy` + `redwood_retention_policy_attachment` for Redwood Private deployments (where supported), plus `modules/retention_policy_private` with regulated defaults examples.
